brief.situation: 10:00 in an outpatient oncology rehabilitation clinic. You are the physical therapist. Mr. Garza, 59, finished radiation for oropharyngeal cancer 14 months ago. His dentist referred him for 'radiation trismus, start jaw stretching'.
handover: He says his jaw opening was 'fine until 2 months ago' and has been getting worse fast; eating is hard and his right ear aches.
Clinic policy: atypical or progressive features after head and neck cancer go back to the treating oncologist before treatment begins.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Each check takes the time on its button. Decide what the findings mean, what to stop or start, and who must know.
Partway through you are asked to write your reasoning. A debrief scores what you did.

parts.label: What and why
parts.criteria: Trismus affects 38-42% after head and neck cancer, but opening under 15 mm, rapid onset a year after treatment, no clicking, ear pain, weight loss and a fixed neck node are atypical and raise concern for recurrence.
parts.modelAnswer: Probably not. Trismus is common after head and neck cancer, but 12 mm, a fast change a year out, no clicking, ear pain, weight loss and a fixed node are red flags for recurrence.

parts.label: What I do
parts.criteria: Holds stretching, calls the treating oncologist the same day, explains and documents.
parts.modelAnswer: No stretching yet. Call his oncologist today, explain to him and document.

scoring.modelReasoning: Trismus is seen in 38-42% of patients after head and neck cancer treatment. Screen and flag atypical features for referral: opening under 15 mm, no clicking history, lymphadenopathy, and a new or rapidly progressive course. Mr. Garza has all of them plus ear pain and weight loss, so refer to his oncologist before treating.
